A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HyperNet Fields research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, tables, and figures can be matched across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-personalization experiments, 3D reconstruction results, and reconstruction-loss and fast-fine-tuning ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds a human preference study reporting 903 evaluations in Section 7 and Table 5.

M1.justification: The time-conditioned hypernetwork, gradient-matching objective, fixed initialization, training algorithm, and inference procedure are unchanged. Figure 2 redraws the supervision pathway without changing the procedure specified in Algorithm 1 and Equations 2–4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CelebA-HQ and AFHQ personalization, image-conditioned Objaverse reconstruction, and point-cloud-conditioned ShapeNet reconstruction. The added survey evaluates personalized images under already represented prompt conditions; no additional dataset, domain, or task coverage is documented.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 and the existing qualitative comparisons is unchanged. The new preference survey uses DreamBooth and Textual Inversion, both already evaluated against the proposed method.

E3.justification: Section 7 adds a human evaluation protocol: participants choose a preferred generation method given a conditioning image and prompt, with 903 evaluations reported. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, preprocessing, and automatic metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The reconstruction-loss and fast-fine-tuning ablations, early-training examples, and optimization-trajectory analysis are retained. The failure example moves from Figure 8 to Figure 12. The new survey supplies comparative preferences without adding a separate ablation, sensitivity test, or controlled robustness analysis.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests are added. The survey reports aggregate preference percentages and an evaluation sample size, without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports preferences of 43.5% for the proposed method, 35.1% for DreamBooth, and 21.4% for Textual Inversion. Tables 1–4, the trajectory plot, and existing qualitative results are unchanged; the survey supplies additional findings under a different evaluation protocol.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the gradient-matching derivation, and the initialization constraint are unchanged. No new mathematical assumption, theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and main conclusion retain the same claims: learning weight trajectories without precomputed target weights, reducing training overhead, and achieving competitive personalization and 3D reconstruction results.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges memory inefficiency from producing one output per target-network weight and proposes compact adapter representations as future work. Section 7 expands the earlier concern about face-recognition scores on stylized images and interprets human preferences as stronger evidence of identity preservation.

D1.justification: The architecture, hyperparameters, data-processing instructions, hardware, and training-time disclosures in Sections 3.4 and 4 are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: V2 adds HyperFields and HyperMAML to the hypernetwork discussion, incorporates shortcut and consistency trajectory models into the denoising discussion, and cites Dravid et al. for compact adapter representations. These extend the existing positioning; other reference changes largely correct metadata or remove duplication.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and phrasing edits, particularly in related work, and expands the limitations paragraph and Section 7 with the survey discussion. The overall section organization and methodological narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to display weight differences and an explicit MSE-loss block. Table 5 is added, appendix tables shift, and the reconstruction-loss failure figure moves to the final page as Figure 12. Existing qualitative image content is retained despite renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 adds human preference evidence relevant to the previously acknowledged limitations of automatic face metrics, explicitly identifies a memory-scaling limitation, and broadens related-work context. These improve validation and qualification of the unchanged method. The gain remains limited because the survey omits participant counts, detailed sampling procedures, and uncertainty estimates, while existing benchmark evidence is unchanged.
